headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the costs of grid upgrades and capacity from residential ratepayers to large energy users, such as data centers, potentially lowering household electricity bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, environmental groups, Governor's administration, Dominion Energy (initially).
opponents: Large energy users (data centers, industrial companies), business lobbies, Data Center Coalition.
news_headline: Virginia Shifts Grid Costs to Data Centers, Saving Residents
news_summary: Virginia regulators have ordered data centers to pay for transmission infrastructure exclusively serving their facilities, a move supported by the Governor's administration to save residential ratepayers hundreds of millions of dollars. This decision ensures that the booming data center industry shoulders more of the grid upgrade costs it generates.

headline: Require Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This legislation mandates that water suppliers report the total volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and providing state regulators with better information for water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, state agencies (DEQ), Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden/potential scrutiny), business lobbies.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, making the information publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to address concerns about data centers' significant water consumption and provide credible data for informed decision-making.

headline: Establish Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools for new high-energy data centers and allows localities to require assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, local government associations, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center industry, developers, business lobbies.
news_headline: Virginia Law Boosts Data Center Siting Transparency
news_summary: HB 153, now law, requires site assessments for noise impacts from new high-energy data centers on nearby residential areas and schools. It also empowers localities to demand assessments on potential impacts to water, agriculture, and historic resources, increasing transparency in data center development.
